articles.title: Delta Pilot Suffers Medical Emergency Moments After Take-Off
articles.description: Lucas Jackson/Reuters A Delta Air Lines flight was forced to land moments after taking off when its first officer suffered a sudden medical emergency. Shortly after departing Minneapolis en route to Orlando, Delta Flight 1208 requested and was granted “priority handling” to return to MSP on Monday. Air Traffic Control recordings published by FlightRadar24 reported there had been a “potential pilot incapacitation” onboard the 25-year-old Boeing 757. The captain said that the plane, which had 190 people onboard, “wanted to return immediately.” ATC could then be heard telling Minneapolis airport’s maintenance team that the pilot in question had suffered “numbness in the arms and legs and a racing heart rate in the high 100s.” In a statement from Delta to NBC5 Chicago , the airline wrote that there was a “medical issue involving a pilot.” Delta said that “the crew followed established procedures to return to MSP, where the aircraft landed safely.” It continued, “As safety comes first at Delta, we are focused on supporting the pilot and our customers to ensure onward travel.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by AviationCircle (@theaviationcircle) Read it at NBC5 Chicago Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: Pilot’s Drunken Flight Sparks Fighter Jet Chase and Scary Landing
articles.description: Hungarian National Police A 24-year-old Hungarian man allegedly stole a small plane while drunk, triggering a fighter jet response before crash-landing in a sunflower field. Hungarian police said the man took the Cessna 172 from Kalocsa airport, around 90 miles south of Budapest, and flew briefly before making an emergency landing in the field near Gerjen in Tolna County. Hungarian Defense Minister Dr. Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said the aircraft entered the airspace near Paks Nuclear Power Plant, the country’s only commercial nuclear facility, causing two fighter jets to be scrambled. Despite the rough landing, authorities said the man only suffered minor injuries. He reportedly walked away from the aircraft, and, according to police, then tried to steal a car from a motorist who stopped to help him. Police arrested the man before he could flee. He was taken into custody while investigators examine whether drugs, in addition to alcohol, were involved. It’s unclear whether the man had any flying experience. Read it at People Magazine Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: 2 terrorists killed in Lakki Marwat IBO: police
articles.description: LAKKI MARWAT: Two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Lakki Marwat district, police said. Qudratullah Khan, the spokesperson for the district police officer in Lakki Marwat, said in a statement that the operation was jointly conducted by police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) personnel after receiving “credible information about the presence of Fitna-al-Khawarij terrorists in the mountainous area within the limits of the Lakki City police station”. The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij to refer to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and its affiliates. Khan said, “A fierce gunfight erupted when the law enforcers surrounded the terrorists’ hideout,” adding that two terrorists were killed during the exchange of fire. He said one of the slain terrorists was identified as Mubashir, who was wanted by the CTD in various terrorism-related cases, including bomb blasts. The second individual was yet to be identified. KP’s Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed appreciated the Lakki Marwat police and CTD personnel for conducting a “successful and result-oriented” operation. He added that the police were “fully determined to completely root out the scourge of terrorism”. KP, including Lakki Marwat, has been facing security challenges, and according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies tracking violence and terrorism, the province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, representing an increase of 105pc. The number of people injured rose from 60 to 98. Security personnel deaths in mainland KP increased from 12 to 38, while terrorist deaths rose by 192pc, from 37 to 108. Civilian deaths, however, declined by 73pc, falling from 26 in June to seven in July. One member of a peace committee was also killed in the province. Data showed a slight decline in overall deaths in the merged districts of KP, formerly known as Fata. The region recorded 79 deaths in July, compared with 85 in June. The number of people injured in the merged districts declined by 37pc, from 60 to 38. Security personnel deaths increased from six to 11, while terrorist deaths declined by 24pc, from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13.

articles.title: Russia attacks kill at least 12 in Kyiv region
articles.description: Ukrainian authorities say that Russia has launched a large aerial assault on Ukraine’s capital and surrounding region. The attacks from Monday evening to early Tuesday killed at least 12 people and wounded more than a dozen others including three children. The strikes mark the sixth straight day of heavy Russian attacks on Kyiv, an unprecedented stretch since Russia invaded over 41⁄2 years ago. Ukrainian officials say Moscow aims to disrupt daily life. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the death toll which included an Indian citizen. The Russian Defense Ministry said that the assault targeted military-related infrastructure. Ukraine’s air force said that Russia used various missiles and drones with the main targets the Kyiv and Odesa regions.

articles.title: Aviation workers in Kenya end strike that paralyzed capital airport
articles.description: Kenyan aviation workers have called off a strike that paralyzed air traffic for two days at the main international airport in the capital Nairobi. The go-slow strike ended Tuesday after the Kenya Aviation Workers Union reached an agreement with Kenya Airports Authority and others. The strike has left many travelers stranded by cancellations and flight delays. Unionized members alleged unfair staff hiring practices, poor compensation and proposed changes to the management of Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport.
